limitations: Finite horizon four; independent sign-amplitude representation with amplitude support ratio below two; no global characterization over all real-valued 3-wise independent laws; parity conditioning itself is classical; older dependent-fluctuation literature leaves residual originality uncertainty; no independent audit has been performed.
scientific_summary: For four fair 3-wise independent signs, the joint law has one remaining parameter theta, the fourth-order product moment. With iid non-atomic positive amplitudes supported in [a,b] with b<2a, strong four-step persistence is exactly (35-5 theta)/128, so two exchangeable continuous laws with every proper subset iid can have persistence 15/64 and 5/16.
